hero.headline: Anthropic raises $65 billion at $965 billion valuation ahead of IPO
hero.body:
Anthropic has closed a $65 billion Series H funding round at a post-money valuation of $965 billion, the AI startup announced. The round could be the company's final private fundraise before a planned initial public offering.

The fundraising milestone marks one of the largest venture capital rounds in technology history. The valuation positions Anthropic as one of the most valuable private companies globally, approaching the trillion-dollar threshold that only a handful of public companies have reached.

The Series H round reflects continued investor confidence in AI development despite broader questions about the sector's long-term profitability and sustainability. Anthropic competes with OpenAI, Google, and other major players in the race to develop advanced artificial intelligence systems.

The company has not disclosed which investors participated in the round or provided a timeline for a potential IPO. Previous funding rounds have drawn backing from Google, Salesforce Ventures, and other major technology and investment firms.

Anthropic develops AI models designed to be safer and more controllable than competing systems. The company was founded by former OpenAI executives and has positioned itself as taking a more cautious approach to AI development.

The near-trillion-dollar valuation comes as AI companies face mounting costs for computing power, talent acquisition, and infrastructure. Training advanced AI models requires significant capital investment in specialized hardware and energy resources.

An IPO would allow Anthropic to access public markets for additional capital while providing liquidity to early investors and employees. The timing of any public offering will depend on market conditions and the company's readiness to meet regulatory requirements for publicly traded companies.

cards.headline: US and Iran agree to tentative ceasefire extension and Strait of Hormuz opening
cards.body:
The United States and Iran have reached a tentative agreement to extend their ceasefire for two months and reopen the Strait of Hormuz, according to White House confirmation. The deal requires approval from President Trump before it can take effect.

The agreement establishes a 60-day memorandum of understanding that would create a framework for broader nuclear program negotiations between the two nations. This follows a two-week conditional ceasefire deal agreed to on Tuesday evening, which came after last-minute diplomatic intervention by Pakistan. The ceasefire prevented military action that had been threatened before a Trump deadline.

The Strait of Hormuz represents a critical waterway for global oil shipping and has been a significant point of tension between the countries. Opening this passage could have major implications for energy markets and international trade. Reports of the potential breakthrough have already influenced global oil prices, which fell following the announcement of the extended ceasefire talks.

The opening of the waterway addresses widespread concerns about disruptions to shipping routes that transport a substantial portion of the world's oil supply. The arrangement also comes amid energy cost concerns in other countries, with energy bills set to rise for millions as the impact of the Iran conflict continues to affect global markets.

The ceasefire extension aims to maintain regional stability while both nations pursue diplomatic discussions. The memorandum provides a structured path for continued dialogue over the coming two months, giving negotiators time to work toward longer-term solutions.

However, the agreement faces complications. Iran released two different versions of a 10-point plan intended as the basis for negotiations. The Farsi version included language about "acceptance of enrichment" for Iran's nuclear program, which was absent from the English translation shared with journalists. This discrepancy created uncertainty around the ceasefire process.

Trump has characterized Iran's 10-point plan as a "workable basis on which to negotiate," suggesting openness to the diplomatic path forward.

It is important to note that Israel has confirmed its backing for the US ceasefire with Iran, though Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu stated that the agreement does not cover Israeli military operations against Hezbollah in Lebanon.

The tentative nature of the agreement means negotiations could still face obstacles before implementation. Presidential approval represents a required step before the arrangement can take effect. Whether this ceasefire extension leads to sustained peace depends on implementation and follow-through from both governments over the coming weeks and months.

cards.headline: Judge declines to block Trump executive order restricting mail-in voting
cards.body:
A federal judge in Washington, D.C. has declined to temporarily block President Trump's executive order that restricts mail-in voting. The decision allows the administration to continue implementing the voting restrictions while legal challenges proceed through the courts.

Democrats filed a lawsuit seeking an immediate preliminary injunction to halt the executive order. The judge's refusal to grant this request represents a setback for Democratic efforts to overturn the voting restrictions in the near term.

The executive order has drawn criticism from voting rights advocates who argue it could limit ballot access for certain voters. Supporters of the measure contend it addresses legitimate election security concerns.

It is important to note that the judge's decision applies only to the request for an immediate preliminary injunction. The judge did not rule on the underlying merits of the case. The legal challenge to the executive order will continue moving through the federal court system, with both sides expected to present their full arguments as the litigation proceeds.

Mail-in voting expanded significantly in recent years, particularly during the pandemic when many voters sought safer ways to cast ballots. The rules governing absentee and mail-in voting vary considerably by state. However, federal executive actions can influence how states administer their elections.

The Trump administration can continue putting the voting restrictions into effect while Democrats pursue their legal challenge in court. Another judge may issue a ruling on the order soon, according to reporting on the case.

Access to mail-in voting has become a point of significant dispute between the two major political parties. Democrats generally support expanded access to mail voting, while Republicans have raised concerns about election fraud. However, widespread fraud in mail voting has not been documented by election officials or researchers.

The outcome of this case could have important implications for how Americans vote in upcoming elections. Lower court decisions on executive orders can be appealed, and the case may ultimately reach higher courts if either side chooses to challenge an unfavorable ruling.

For now, the Trump administration's voting restrictions remain in place as the legal process unfolds. The fact that a judge did not immediately block the order suggests the court found the legal challenge faced significant hurdles, though the judge has not made any final determinations about whether the executive order is lawful or constitutional.

The case demonstrates the ongoing tension over voting access between Republican and Democratic leaders, a conflict that has intensified in recent election cycles and continues to play out in courtrooms across the country.

cards.headline: Supreme Court rules for Mississippi death row inmate in racial bias case
cards.teaser: The Supreme Court sided with a Mississippi man on death row in a case involving racial bias.
cards.body:
Rewritten Card:

The US Supreme Court ruled 5-4 in favor of Terry Pitchford, a Black man on death row in Mississippi, who challenged his capital murder conviction on racial bias grounds. Pitchford was 18 when convicted and argued that Black jurors were improperly excluded from his trial.

The decision represents a significant victory for Pitchford in his legal battle over jury composition and potential discrimination in his case proceedings.

cards.headline: Treasury launches Trump Accounts app for $1,000 per child federal investment program
cards.teaser: The mobile application allows parents to manage federally funded investment accounts created for children.
cards.body:
The US Treasury Department rolled out a mobile application to manage Trump Accounts, a program that provides $1,000 in federal investment funds for each child. The app launched nationwide and allows parents and guardians to access and monitor the accounts created under the program.

Treasury Secretary Bessent announced the app's availability. The program establishes individual investment accounts with government-provided seed capital intended to grow over time. The mobile platform provides account holders with tools to track the investments and manage account details. The initiative represents a new federal approach to building wealth for children through government-funded investment accounts.

cards.headline: Canadian Prime Minister Calls for New U.S. Relationship
cards.teaser: Prime Minister Carney said in a New York speech that Canada's distancing from the U.S. benefits American interests.
cards.body:
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney delivered a speech in New York calling for a new partnership between Canada and the United States. He emphasized the need for greater economic cooperation and a "true partnership" that reimagines how the two countries work together in sectors facing global competition.

Carney framed Canada's approach as beneficial to American interests, advocating for fresh collaboration between the neighboring nations on economic matters going forward.

cards.headline: Israel Strikes Beirut in Targeted Attack
cards.teaser: Israel conducted a targeted strike on the Lebanese capital, which had been largely spared during recent hostilities.
cards.body:
Israel conducted a targeted strike on Beirut, marking a significant escalation in the Lebanese capital. Until this attack, the city had largely avoided military operations even as the recent conflict continued elsewhere and both Israel and Hezbollah accused each other of breaching last month's ceasefire.

The strike represents a shift in the scope of Israeli military operations in Lebanon, expanding beyond areas that had previously borne the brunt of the fighting.

hero.headline: U.S. and Iran Near Agreement to Reopen Strait of Hormuz
hero.body:
U.S. officials say they are closing in on an arrangement with Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, though President Trump has not yet approved the emerging framework. The agreement could extend the current cease-fire and lead to more substantial negotiations between the two countries.

The framework would allow both nations to continue discussions on nuclear issues and other matters while the strait remains open. U.S. officials described the arrangement as a potential foundation for broader talks, though they emphasized that Trump's signature remains necessary before any deal takes effect.

The Strait of Hormuz, a critical shipping channel for global oil supplies, has been at the center of tensions during the conflict between the United States and Iran. The proposed arrangement represents the most significant diplomatic progress since the cease-fire began.

However, recent developments suggest the negotiations remain fragile. Iran's parliamentary speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf said reopening the strait would be "impossible" while the U.S. and Israel continue what he called "flagrant" breaches of the ceasefire, including a U.S. naval blockade. Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps seized two ships attempting to cross the strait, the first seizures since the conflict began. The U.S. had previously fired on and seized an Iranian cargo vessel and boarded an Iranian oil tanker.

The closure of the Strait of Hormuz has triggered a global economic crisis. Approximately 20 percent of the world's oil and liquefied gas passed through the waterway during peacetime. About 20,000 seafarers and 2,000 ships remain stranded, according to the International Maritime Organization. Countries dependent on Gulf oil have faced severe shortages of fuel and raw materials. Germany halved its 2026 growth forecast to 0.5 percent, while Greece announced 500 million euros in additional aid for households and farmers.

White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt stated that Trump was "satisfied" with the naval blockade and believed Iran was in a "very weak position." She said the U.S. was "completely strangling their economy through this blockade, they're losing 500 million a day."

Planned peace talks in Islamabad failed to materialize. A Pakistani official said the country had prepared extensively for negotiations, with the U.S. delegation led by Vice President JD Vance expected to participate. However, Iran never publicly accepted the invitation and the U.S. delegation never left Washington.

The proposed framework focuses specifically on reopening the strait while leaving more complex issues for future negotiations. The timing of any final decision remains uncertain, as both Trump and Iran's leadership must weigh domestic and strategic considerations.

Neither side appears interested in returning to full-scale conflict, according to observers, despite recent military exchanges and the ongoing blockade standoff.

cards.headline: 16 Students Die in Kenya School Fire
cards.teaser: A fire at a Kenyan school killed 16 students, with parents waiting for news about their children hours after the blaze.
cards.body:
A fire swept through a dormitory at Utumishi girls academy in Gilgil, Nakuru county, killing at least 16 students. The blaze broke out just after midnight at the school located about 76 miles northwest of Nairobi in Kenya's Rift Valley.

The incident has intensified concerns about safety standards at educational facilities across the country. Parents gathered at the scene, anxiously seeking updates about their children in the hours following the fire.

cards.headline: Gaza Strike Kills at Least Five Children
cards.teaser: At least five children were killed in a strike on Gaza City that appeared to target a Hamas commander.
cards.body:
Israeli forces struck a residential building in Gaza City, killing Mohammed Odeh, the newly appointed head of Hamas's military wing, along with his wife and two children. Hospital officials reported that several people, including at least five children total, died in the strike.

The operation is part of Israel's ongoing military campaign against Hamas leadership in Gaza, conducted alongside separate operations in the region as tensions remain elevated across multiple fronts.

cards.headline: Justice Department Opens Criminal Investigation Into Trump Accuser E Jean Carroll
cards.teaser: The Justice Department launched a criminal probe examining whether columnist E Jean Carroll lied about lawsuit funding.
cards.body:
The U.S. Justice Department has launched a criminal investigation into E Jean Carroll, the former columnist who accused President Trump of sexual assault. Investigators are examining whether Carroll provided false information regarding the funding of her civil lawsuit against Trump.

Carroll previously secured civil verdicts against Trump in cases involving defamation and sexual abuse allegations. The criminal investigation marks a significant escalation in the legal dispute between the two parties.

cards.headline: Three Injured in Stabbing at Swiss Train Station
cards.teaser: A 31-year-old Swiss man was arrested after three people were injured in a stabbing at a train station.
cards.body:
A 31-year-old Swiss man has been arrested following a stabbing incident at a Swiss train station that left three people injured. Police responded to the scene, where portions of the station were cordoned off as part of the security response.

Images from the incident show the affected areas of the station secured by authorities.

cards.headline: Portugal Sets May Temperature Record as Europe Faces Heat Wave
cards.teaser: Portugal broke its hottest May day record as a heat wave spreads across Europe, prompting red alerts in Italy.
cards.body:
Portugal recorded its hottest day ever for the month of May as a heat wave affects multiple European countries. Red alerts have been issued in Italy as temperatures climb across the continent.

French students are taking their exams in schools experiencing extreme heat. The unseasonable temperatures have disrupted normal activities across the region as countries respond to the weather conditions.

The framework still requires approval from leaders in both countries. Neither nation appears eager to return to full-scale conflict, despite recent military exchanges between them.

cards.headline: Michigan Governor Gretchen Whitmer will not run for president in 2028
cards.teaser: Michigan Governor Gretchen Whitmer announced she will not seek the presidency in 2028.
cards.body:
Governor Gretchen Whitmer of Michigan said she will not run for president in the 2028 election. The announcement removes a prominent Democrat from the potential field of candidates for the next presidential race.

Whitmer has been a visible figure in Democratic politics and was considered a potential contender for the party's presidential nomination. Her decision not to run will reshape the landscape of candidates as Democrats look ahead to the next election cycle.

cards.headline: FIFA ticket sales practices under investigation following fan complaints
cards.teaser: FIFA is facing an investigation into its World Cup ticket sales after fans complained about the pricing and process for the 2026 tournament.
cards.body:
FIFA is under investigation by authorities in New York and New Jersey over its World Cup ticket sales practices for the 2026 tournament. The governing body faces scrutiny after fans reported being misled about ticket sales and seat locations.

FIFA has long used a distinctive ticketing system for the World Cup without significant controversy. However, prices for the 2026 tournament increased substantially, prompting widespread fan complaints and triggering the current investigation.

A man died after being struck by a train following his escape from a vehicle transporting him to court. The incident took place in Hertfordshire, where police were involved in the transport.

cards.headline: Australian woman charged with traveling to Syria to join Islamic State
cards.teaser: An Australian woman faces charges for allegedly traveling to Syria to join the Islamic State.
cards.body:
Australian authorities have charged a woman with joining the Islamic State in Syria. She returned to Australia eight months prior with her children after being in Lebanon.

The charges relate to her alleged involvement with the terrorist organization. Her case is part of a broader pattern, as several groups of women and children who spent years in Syrian camps have returned to their home countries in recent months.

hero.headline: Fertitta Entertainment to acquire Caesars Entertainment for $18 billion
hero.teaser: Hospitality businessman Tilman Fertitta is purchasing the Las Vegas casino operator in one of the largest deals in gaming industry history.
hero.body:
Caesars Entertainment will be acquired by Fertitta Entertainment in a transaction valued at $17.6 billion to $18 billion, according to multiple reports. The deal transfers ownership of one of the Las Vegas Strip's most recognized casino operators to Tilman Fertitta, who owns the Houston Rockets and operates restaurants and entertainment properties.

The acquisition price was reported as $5.7 billion in one account and between $17.6 billion and $18 billion in others, likely reflecting different calculations of enterprise value versus equity value. Fertitta has ties to the Trump administration and has been expanding his leisure and hospitality holdings. Caesars operates multiple properties in Las Vegas and other gaming markets across the United States.

cards.headline: Federal prosecutors charge Google engineer with insider trading on Polymarket
cards.teaser: A Google employee allegedly used confidential company information to make $1.2 million on prediction market bets.
cards.body:
The U.S. Justice Department has charged Michele Spagnuolo, a 36-year-old Google software engineer, with using insider information to place bets on Polymarket. Prosecutors allege he leveraged confidential data about Google's most-searched list to make wagers on the prediction market platform, earning $1.2 million in profits.

Spagnuolo's case represents a significant enforcement action against insider trading on prediction markets. His arrest follows a similar case one month earlier involving a U.S. Army soldier accused of using classified military information to place Polymarket bets about potential action in Venezuela.

cards.headline: Stock markets reach new highs as Middle East peace progress reported
cards.teaser: The S&P 500 and Nasdaq gained following reports of a possible breakthrough in US-Iran negotiations.
cards.body:
The S&P 500 and Nasdaq indexes rose as investors responded to reports of progress toward a Middle East peace agreement. Oil prices reduced earlier gains after news emerged of a potential US-Iran breakthrough in negotiations. The Dow Jones Industrial Average slipped while the broader market pushed to record levels.

Continued strong corporate earnings supported the market advance. Micron and other memory chip stocks contributed to the rally, with the semiconductor sector helping drive indexes to new highs. Wall Street has seen sustained gains as US companies report profits that exceed analyst expectations across multiple sectors.

cards.headline: Wix to cut 20 percent of workforce in restructuring tied to AI and currency pressures
cards.teaser: The website building platform announced layoffs affecting roughly one-fifth of its employees.
cards.body:
Wix is laying off approximately 20 percent of its staff in a restructuring the company attributes to artificial intelligence developments and exchange rate challenges. The Israeli technology company's CEO cited the need to adapt to changes in the industry and economic pressures affecting the business.

In a memo to employees, the CEO referenced AI as a factor in the decision and acknowledged the company faces difficult choices. The shekel's strength against other currencies was mentioned as contributing to the restructuring. Wix operates a platform that allows users to build websites without coding expertise. The layoffs affect the company's workforce across its global operations.

cards.headline: Patagonia sues drag performer Pattie Gonia over trademark dispute
cards.teaser: The outdoor apparel company claims the performer violated an agreement regarding use of its branding.
cards.body:
Outdoor clothing firm Patagonia filed a trademark infringement lawsuit against drag performer Pattie Gonia, claiming the performer violated an agreement regarding the use of the company's branding in merchandise.

The case centers on whether Pattie Gonia broke the terms of an accord with Patagonia about using the outdoor apparel company's name and branding in commercial products.

cards.teaser: Large exchanges are designing derivative products around AI tokens, treating them as raw material inputs rather than computational outputs.
cards.body:
Major exchanges are developing derivative products that would allow futures trading in AI tokens. The financial instruments represent a shift in how markets view AI-generated outputs, treating them more like commodities such as electricity or bandwidth than software products.

The move reflects growing standardization of AI tokens as tradable assets. Futures contracts would allow buyers and sellers to lock in prices for future delivery of AI computing resources, similar to how commodity markets function for oil, natural gas, and other raw materials.

cards.headline: Prison phone service Pay Tel exposes 300,000 caller ID documents
cards.teaser: Pay Tel secured publicly exposed data after security researchers discovered a leak containing drivers licenses and inmate communications.
cards.body:
A security lapse at Pay Tel, which operates phone services in correctional facilities, exposed over 300,000 callers' driver's licenses and other identification documents online. The breach also included inmate communications. Security researchers discovered the publicly accessible data and notified the company.

Pay Tel secured the exposed information after learning of the leak. The company requires inmates and people calling them to provide identification documents for account setup and call monitoring purposes.

cards.headline: Illinois passes AI safety law as Trump administration loses regulatory control
cards.teaser: Anthropic and OpenAI support Illinois legislation requiring safety testing, marking a state-level challenge to federal AI policy.
cards.body:
Illinois has passed a landmark AI regulation law that includes mandatory safety testing requirements. The legislation reduces federal control over AI oversight under the Trump administration, with both Anthropic and OpenAI expressing support for the state-level approach.

The law represents a shift toward decentralized AI governance as individual states establish their own regulatory frameworks. Companies operating in Illinois will need to comply with the state's safety testing protocols regardless of federal policy.

cards.headline: Anthropic releases Opus 4.8 with agent coordination tool
cards.teaser: The new AI model includes Dynamic Workflows, a tool designed to coordinate multiple subagents working together.
cards.body:
Anthropic has released Opus 4.8, an updated version of its AI model that includes a new feature called Dynamic Workflows. The tool allows users to coordinate swarms of subagents, enabling multiple AI systems to work on complex tasks simultaneously.

The release adds to Anthropic's product lineup as the company approaches a potential IPO. Dynamic Workflows represents an attempt to make AI systems more capable of handling tasks that require multiple steps or specialized subtasks working in parallel.

cards.headline: Startup Corgi raises $106 million at doubled valuation in three weeks
cards.teaser: The company's valuation jumped to $2.6 billion just three weeks after its previous funding round, with the same investors participating in both.
cards.body:
Corgi has secured $106 million in funding at a $2.6 billion valuation, doubling its worth from just three weeks prior. The same investor group participated in both rounds, an unusual circumstance given the dramatic valuation jump.

While rapid funding rounds with significant step-ups have become more common in the AI sector, doubling a company's value in such a compressed timeframe with identical investors is noteworthy enough to warrant scrutiny.

cards.headline: Intel launches Arc G3 processors for handheld gaming devices
cards.teaser: Intel introduces new chips designed for portable gaming PCs, competing with AMD in the handheld market.
cards.body:
Intel has released its Arc G3 line of processors aimed at handheld gaming devices. The chips bring up to 14 cores and Arc B390 graphics to portable gaming systems, marking Intel's entry into a market segment where AMD has been dominant.

Acer announced the Predator Atlas 8 as one of the first handheld gaming devices to use the new Intel processors. The Arc G3 represents Intel's attempt to establish a presence in the growing category of portable gaming hardware.

hero.headline: Four-time Stanley Cup champion Claude Lemieux dies at 60
hero.body:
Claude Lemieux, a four-time Stanley Cup champion who played 21 seasons in the National Hockey League, has died at age 60. Multiple sources confirmed his death.

Lemieux won Stanley Cup championships with three different teams during his career. He captured titles with the Montreal Canadiens, New Jersey Devils twice, and Colorado Avalanche. His ability to perform in playoff situations made him one of the most successful postseason players of his era.

TMZ reported that Lemieux died by suicide. The circumstances surrounding his death remain limited in publicly available information.

Lemieux played for six NHL franchises over his career, which spanned from the mid-1980s to the mid-2000s. He was known for his physical style of play and his production during the Stanley Cup playoffs. His playoff performances often exceeded his regular season statistics.

The right winger played more than 1,200 regular season games in the NHL. He also appeared in over 230 playoff games, scoring crucial goals in championship runs. His final Stanley Cup victory came with the Devils in 2000.

Lemieux's death comes as a loss to the hockey community. He remained connected to the sport after his retirement from professional play. Multiple NHL teams and players acknowledged his passing.

The NHL and individual teams have not yet released formal statements about memorial plans or tributes. Lemieux's career statistics and championship wins place him among notable players from his generation.

His four Stanley Cup rings represent championships won across different franchises and eras of NHL hockey. The consistency of his playoff performances contributed to each team's championship success.

cards.headline: New York and New Jersey investigate FIFA over World Cup ticket pricing
cards.teaser: State attorneys general have subpoenaed FIFA over ticket sales practices and pricing for the upcoming World Cup.
cards.body:
New York and New Jersey have subpoenaed FIFA as part of an investigation into the organization's World Cup ticket sales practices. Fans have reported being misled about ticket availability and seat locations, prompting the probe by both states.

FIFA's ticketing approach for the 2026 World Cup, which will be partially hosted in the New York and New Jersey region, has generated widespread outrage over soaring prices. The investigation examines whether FIFA's pricing and sales practices violated consumer protection laws.

cards.headline: World number one Jannik Sinner loses in second round at French Open
cards.teaser: Top-ranked tennis player Jannik Sinner fell to Juan Manuel Cerundolo in a second round upset at the French Open.
cards.body:
Jannik Sinner suffered a second round defeat to Juan Manuel Cerundolo at the French Open in one of the biggest shocks in recent years at the tournament. The world number one said he could not find any energy during the match.

Sinner dismissed the Paris heat as an excuse for his performance. The early exit marks a significant upset for the top seed at Roland Garros. Cerundolo advanced to the third round with the victory.

cards.headline: Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart addresses team after Trump rally controversy
cards.teaser: Quarterback Jaxson Dart spoke to the Giants locker room following controversy over his introduction at a Donald Trump political rally.
cards.body:
Jaxson Dart addressed the New York Giants locker room after introducing Donald Trump at a political rally sparked controversy within the team. Sources indicated the team worked through the drama surrounding the incident.

Abdul Carter was not present for the team meeting where Dart spoke. The gathering came after the quarterback's appearance at the Trump event drew attention. The Giants dealt with the situation internally as the roster navigated the political controversy.

cards.headline: Patriots and Eagles negotiate compensation in potential A.J. Brown trade
cards.teaser: The New England Patriots and Philadelphia Eagles have discussed trade terms for wide receiver A.J. Brown, with disagreement over compensation.
cards.body:
The Patriots and Eagles have grappled over compensation in ongoing trade talks involving wide receiver A.J. Brown. Reports indicate the two teams could potentially swap draft picks as part of a deal.

Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts described his relationship with Brown as really good despite the trade speculation. Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel addressed the situation in a press conference. CBS Sports analysis suggests the Eagles and Brown are headed for a split.

cards.headline: New Zealand bowler Nathan Smith takes six wickets against Ireland
cards.teaser: Nathan Smith claimed a career-best 6-40 as New Zealand dominated the second day of their Test match against Ireland in Belfast.
cards.body:
New Zealand took control of their one-off Test against Ireland on the second day at Stormont in Belfast. Nathan Smith was the standout performer with the ball, claiming an international career best of 6-40 as the visitors dominated proceedings.

Smith's exceptional bowling display put New Zealand in a commanding position in the match.

cards.headline: Ronda Rousey says she would defeat Holly Holm in rematch but will not return
cards.teaser: Former UFC champion Ronda Rousey responded to rematch talk with Holly Holm, claiming she would win but insisting she remains retired.
cards.body:
Ronda Rousey said she would clean the clock of Holly Holm in a potential rematch but confirmed she is retired from mixed martial arts. The statement came in response to Holm discussing a possible second fight.

Holm had reacted to Rousey beating Gina Carano and said she highly doubts Rousey would ever want a rematch. Rousey claimed she could re-write UFC history in a second bout with Holm. Holm indicated she would be open to fighting Rousey again.

hero.headline: Stranger Things Ends as Most-Watched Series of 2025-26 TV Season
hero.body:
Stranger Things concluded its final season as the most-watched television series of the 2025-26 season, averaging 32.9 million viewers over 35 days across all platforms, according to Nielsen's multiplatform ranker.

The Netflix thriller topped the measurement system that combines streaming, broadcast, and cable viewership data into a unified comparison. Nielsen introduced this approach last year to create standardized metrics regardless of distribution platform.

The show's final season dropped its first four episodes on Wednesday after three years in development. The release proved so anticipated that Netflix crashed within minutes, with the outage tracker Downdetector recording more than 14,000 reports in the US. Netflix reported that some members experienced brief streaming issues on TV devices, but service recovered for all accounts within five minutes. The outage followed similar incidents during major events like the Mike Tyson versus Jake Paul boxing match and a Love is Blind reunion in 2024.

Series co-creator Ross Duffer said on Instagram that Netflix had increased bandwidth by 30 percent to prevent a crash. The day before the finale dropped, all previous Stranger Things seasons appeared simultaneously on Netflix's top 10 shows chart for the first time in the platform's history.

The final season features a time jump to account for how quickly the show's young stars have aged since their debuts nearly a decade ago. Millie Bobby Brown, Finn Wolfhard, Noah Schnapp, Caleb McLaughlin, and Gaten Matarazzo have anchored the cast since the beginning, alongside adult actors Joe Keery, Natalia Dyer, Winona Ryder, and David Harbour. Sadie Sink, who joined in season two, described filming her final scenes as emotionally comparable to "saying goodbye to your childhood."

Co-creators Matt and Ross Duffer have shared that the new season will feature "the most violent death of any season." The show, set in the 1980s, follows residents of the fictional Indiana town of Hawkins after a young girl with psychokinetic abilities opens a gateway to another dimension called the Upside Down.

The 32.9 million average viewer count represents those who watched during Nielsen's 35-day measurement window, accounting for how modern audiences consume television through delayed viewing and binge-watching patterns common with streaming services.

The series' performance as the season's most-watched program demonstrates the ability of streaming platforms to generate substantial viewership numbers. Stranger Things has remained a cornerstone property for Netflix since its 2016 debut and continues demonstrating its status as one of the defining television programs of its era.

cards.headline: Tony Shalhoub to Appear in CBS Drama Einstein
cards.teaser: The actor reunites with Monk creator Andy Breckman for a recurring role in the new series adapted from a German format.
cards.body:
Tony Shalhoub has joined the cast of CBS drama Einstein in a recurring guest star role. The series was developed by Andy Breckman from a German format.

The collaboration reunites Shalhoub with Breckman, who previously created the USA Network series Monk. Shalhoub starred in that show for eight seasons and appeared in a followup television movie.

cards.headline: Mary McDonnell Joins Baywatch Reboot Cast
cards.teaser: The actress will play the mother of Stephen Amell's character in a recurring guest role.
cards.body:
Mary McDonnell has been cast in the Baywatch reboot as a recurring guest star. She will play Gayle, the mother of protagonist Hobie Buchannon, portrayed by Stephen Amell.

The character is described as a sophisticated woman with a wryly funny presence who cares deeply for her family. She remains supportive even when her family members are uncertain about needing her help.

cards.headline: Ken Brown Named Managing Editor at CNBC
cards.teaser: The veteran financial journalist will oversee digital editorial operations and help shape overall strategy at the business news outlet.
cards.body:
Ken Brown is joining CNBC as managing editor of digital and editorial strategy. He will report to CNBC editor in chief David Cho and begin his new role on June 8.

Brown will oversee the business news outlet's digital editorial operations and contribute to overall editorial strategy development. He brings years of experience in financial journalism to the position.

cards.headline: Artists Clash Over Trump Freedom 250 Concert
cards.teaser: Several musicians have announced conflicting decisions about performing at the event, with some dropping out and others confirming participation.
cards.body:
Multiple artists have responded publicly to the announcement of Trump's Freedom 250 concert with varying reactions. Freedom Williams of C + C Music Factory posted an expletive-filled rant, while Morris Day stated it was a no for him. Young MC dropped out of the lineup.

Vanilla Ice said he would participate in the event. The conflicting responses from artists created confusion about the final concert lineup.

cards.headline: M&M Partners With Love Island USA for Eighth Season
cards.teaser: The candy brand will serve as exclusive confectionery partner and release limited-edition play-along packs with custom printed candies.
cards.body:
M&M has partnered with Love Island USA as the exclusive confectionery partner for the show's eighth season. The candy brand is releasing a limited-edition play-along pack to celebrate the collaboration.

The special packs contain game boards and multicolored custom candy printed with recurring one-liners and iconic moments from the reality show. The printed phrases include Got a Text and Bombshell Arrives, among other catchphrases associated with the series.

cards.headline: Netflix Previews Gabriel Martins Film On Behalf of My Son
cards.teaser: The streaming service released the first image from the director's new feature, due to open in the second half of 2026.
cards.body:
Netflix released the first image from On Behalf of My Son, a new feature written and directed by Gabriel Martins. The image shows Rejane Faria as Vicentina, the lead character in the film.

The company released the image from Rio de Janeiro. The film, titled Vicentina Pede Desculpas in Portuguese, is scheduled to open in the second half of 2026. Martins previously directed Mars One.

hero.headline: US and Iran agree to tentative ceasefire extension and Strait of Hormuz opening
hero.body:
The United States and Iran have reached a tentative agreement to extend their ceasefire for two months and reopen the Strait of Hormuz, according to White House confirmation. The deal requires approval from President Trump before it can take effect.

The agreement establishes a 60-day memorandum of understanding that would create a framework for broader nuclear program negotiations between the two nations. This follows a two-week conditional ceasefire deal agreed to on Tuesday evening, which came after last-minute diplomatic intervention by Pakistan. The ceasefire prevented military action that had been threatened before a Trump deadline.

The Strait of Hormuz represents a critical waterway for global oil shipping and has been a significant point of tension between the countries. Opening this passage could have major implications for energy markets and international trade. Reports of the potential breakthrough have already influenced global oil prices, which fell following the announcement of the extended ceasefire talks.

The opening of the waterway addresses widespread concerns about disruptions to shipping routes that transport a substantial portion of the world's oil supply. The arrangement also comes amid energy cost concerns in other countries, with energy bills set to rise for millions as the impact of the Iran conflict continues to affect global markets.

The ceasefire extension aims to maintain regional stability while both nations pursue diplomatic discussions. The memorandum provides a structured path for continued dialogue over the coming two months, giving negotiators time to work toward longer-term solutions.

However, the agreement faces complications. Iran released two different versions of a 10-point plan intended as the basis for negotiations. The Farsi version included language about "acceptance of enrichment" for Iran's nuclear program, which was absent from the English translation shared with journalists. This discrepancy created uncertainty around the ceasefire process.

Trump has characterized Iran's 10-point plan as a "workable basis on which to negotiate," suggesting openness to the diplomatic path forward.

It is important to note that Israel has confirmed its backing for the US ceasefire with Iran, though Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu stated that the agreement does not cover Israeli military operations against Hezbollah in Lebanon.

The tentative nature of the agreement means negotiations could still face obstacles before implementation. Presidential approval represents a required step before the arrangement can take effect. Whether this ceasefire extension leads to sustained peace depends on implementation and follow-through from both governments over the coming weeks and months.

cards.headline: Supreme Court rules for Mississippi death row inmate in racial bias case
cards.teaser: Terry Pitchford argued for two decades that his conviction was invalid due to racially biased jury selection.
cards.body:
The Supreme Court ruled 5-4 in favor of Terry Pitchford, a Black man on Mississippi's death row who challenged his conviction on grounds of racial bias in jury selection. Pitchford, who was 18 when convicted of murder, argued that Black jurors were excluded from his trial, undermining the validity of his conviction.

The decision represents a significant ruling on how racial bias claims in jury selection will be handled in future cases. Pitchford has maintained for two decades that the jury selection process was tainted by discrimination.

cards.headline: Michigan Governor Gretchen Whitmer rules out 2028 presidential run
cards.teaser: The term-limited governor had been considered a potential Democratic candidate for the next presidential election.
cards.body:
Michigan Governor Gretchen Whitmer announced she will not run for president in 2028. Whitmer faces term limits after winning two gubernatorial elections in the battleground state.

Political observers had viewed Whitmer as a potential Democratic candidate for the presidential race. Her decision removes one name from early speculation about the Democratic field for the next election cycle.

cards.headline: Southern Democratic chairs urge South Carolina to hold first 2028 primary
cards.teaser: Democratic Party leaders from five Southern states wrote to DNC Chair Ken Martin requesting South Carolina lead the primary calendar.
cards.body:
Democratic Party chairs from Alabama, Mississippi, Louisiana, Arkansas and West Virginia sent a letter to Democratic National Committee Chair Ken Martin advocating for South Carolina to hold the first primary in 2028. The request seeks to give South Carolina voters the earliest opportunity to cast ballots in the next presidential primaries.

The letter represents a coordinated effort among Southern state Democratic leadership to influence the party's primary calendar structure. The DNC's Rules and Bylaws Committee will consider primary scheduling as the party plans for the next presidential election cycle.

cards.headline: AARP urges Congress to address Social Security solvency ahead of trustees report
cards.teaser: Officials called for action before the Trump administration releases the annual Social Security board of trustees report.
cards.body:
AARP officials urged Congress to take steps to ensure Social Security remains solvent ahead of the annual board of trustees report from the Trump administration. The organization does not know the exact release date or contents of the upcoming report.

AARP expects the trustees report to address the program's financial sustainability. The organization is calling on lawmakers to act on Social Security funding before receiving the administration's assessment of the program's current state.

cards.headline: Attorney General Pam Bondi to appear before House committee on Epstein matter
cards.teaser: Bondi is scheduled to testify before the House Oversight and Government Reform Committee.
cards.body:
Attorney General Pam Bondi will appear before the House Oversight and Government Reform Committee on Friday. The hearing relates to matters involving Jeffrey Epstein.

Survivors of Epstein's abuse have expressed skepticism about whether the interview will yield answers. Bondi's testimony comes as the committee examines issues related to the Epstein case.

cards.headline: US, Mexico, Canada announce Ebola travel measures for World Cup
cards.teaser: The three host countries implemented public health protocols for travelers from African regions at high risk for Ebola ahead of the June tournament.
cards.body:
The United States, Mexico and Canada announced coordinated public health travel measures for people arriving from parts of Africa at greatest risk from Ebola. The three countries will host the FIFA World Cup beginning in June.

The measures aim to protect citizens and the millions of visitors, fans, athletes and tourists expected for the tournament. The coordinated approach reflects cooperation among the host nations on public health screening for the international event.
